messages.subject: R to nimble function
parts:
Hello!
I am brand new to Nimble and I am trying to convert a spatial integrated population model written in JAGS to Nimble to improve speed and efficiency. However, I am having trouble sorting out one part. In my JAGS model, I have the following loop:

for (i in 1:nsite) {
  for (j in 1:nsite) {
    w_ori_epsilon[i,j] ~ dnorm(0, theta_tau)
    w_ori[i,j] <- ifelse(i==j, 1e-6, exp(-1 * theta_mean * dist[i,j] + w_ori_epsilon[i,j]))
    w[i,j] <- w_ori[i,j] / sum(w_ori[i,1:nsite])
  } # j
} # i

And I am getting an error that says: " R function 'ifelse' has arguments that cannot be evaluated; either the function must be a nimbleFunction or values for the following inputs must be specified as constants in the model: theta_mean,w_ori_epsilon[i, j]."

There does not appear to be an equivalent nimbleFunction to ifelse, and I am not totally clear as to how to specify the two variables noted in the error term as constants. 

My apologies if this is a simple question, I am still trying to wrap by deeply entrenched JAGS mind around Nimble!

messages.subject: Re: R to nimble function
parts:
Hi Meaghan,

Would coding the model like this work? I feel like this is what you are trying to do and avoids the need of an ifelse statement.

w_ori_epsilon[i,i] <- 1e-6   # Fix diagonal to a near zero value
   for (j in (i+1):nsite){
     w_ori_epsilon[i,j] ~ dnorm(0, theta_tau)    # populate one triangle of the variance-covariance matrix
     w_ori_epsilon[j,i] <- w_ori_epsilon[i,j]        # mirror to the other triangle
w_ori[i,j] <- exp(-1 * theta_mean * dist[i,j] + w_ori_epsilon[i,j])

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: R to nimble function
parts:
Hi Meaghan

Welcome to the wonderful world of nimble!!  

One of the great things about nimble is that it gives you the flexibility to write nimble functions that can sit inside your BUGS code. So in your case you can create your own ifelse function and avoid cluttering your BUGS code as a hack.  

Below is an example of how you might write your own ifelse function. In your code, just replace ifelse with myIfElse and your original code should be fine.

I normally have a script called nimbleFunctions.R to store all my nimble functions, and my main script will include the line  source("nimbleFunctions.R") early on so that I can use them. This avoids cluttering my analysis with function definitions.

Cheers
David

library(nimble)

myIfElse <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(condition = integer(0), valueIf=double(0), valueElse=double(0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    if (condition==TRUE) {
      return(valueIf)
    } else {
      return(valueElse)
    }
  }
)

## The following is just a test to verify that the function compiles and gives sensible output.  
## So use myIfElse in your BUGS code, not cIfElse.  
cIfElse <- compileNimble(myIfElse)
a = 2
b = 2
cIfElse(a==b, 123, 456)
cIfElse(a==2*b, 123, 456)
